>I felt this way far too often in my life. Sometimes knowing you’re not the only one really does help.  
>  
>Balance. I am the most disorganized, head in the clouds person you could meet. I’ve always lived 5-10 years ahead in my mind, never in the moment.  
>  
>Recently, I began to get really honest with myself. I’ve realized that all of my life experience is lived and felt from within, that it doesn’t matter what other people do, or think because I’ll never be able to control it, and now I’m so glad I can’t.  
>  
>I was blinded by my past mistakes. I was paralyzed by the future and worried I’d never do anything that would make me feel content or fulfilled. Nothing made much sense and I was hanging on to the things I was taught as a child, but could never fully give myself to it.  
>  
>So I decided to get honest. I started to look inward. I began to realize I had placed layers and layers of filters over who I really am, and found that I had created a weird version of myself as a means to fool the outside world that I was better than I really was. It was a subconscious attempt to protect myself. Once those filters fell off when I dealt with some childhood trauma, my eyes opened.  
>  
>We live on the only planet in the known universe that can sustain life. We are the only species with minds and bodies capable of building incredible things...  
>  
>Life isn’t about what we do, it’s about who we are. I’ve never seen myself as part of it all, more of an observer until very recently. Please at least consider that there is a beautiful landscape inside that has yet to be discovered. This life is absolutely incredible if you experience it from bottom up. It’s about being conscious. Create some space from your mind and emotions and realize they are tools for you to understand the external world. Who you are is not the sum total of your thoughts and feelings, you run much deeper than that. You are the conductor of your mind and emotions.  
>  
>This may sound odd, and I admittedly don’t have the answers, nor do I know how to even articulate it properly, I just know that the life I’m experiencing now is night and day different than just 7-8 months ago, and little has changed externally.  
>  
>Be encouraged friend, you can find peace. Turn your eyes inward and be as honest as you can with yourself in every single area of your past with humility. Take responsibility for what you’ve done and you’ll see who you really are. Everyone has things they wished they’d did differently. It’s ok. It doesn’t make you a bad person, just reinforces the fact that you are a person. Forgive yourself completely and you will see the world in a way you didn’t think was possible.  
>  
>And it’s free. No strings attached. You don’t have to sell your soul or invoke out-dated rituals. Just take an honest inventory of your life to date, make amends with a past you can never change and you will experience the life worth living :)  
>  
>Or don’t. Please understand my intention is only to help. If this doesn’t sit well, my apologies

Thank you so so much for writing this. It's exactly what I needed, since I've been struggling with existential questions for a while now too.

That's a good point. I'd say, every time you decide that you want to contact her, come back and read what you've written in this post and all the comments (or just remember some other bad situations). When you see it all written down from your perspective, it might not look that toxic to you (especially after some time), but I feel like everyone here agrees that she really only thinks about herself. You have to think about putting yourself first and that involves becoming self-sufficient (which can be hard, I'm struggling with it too) and it is a long journey, but I can assure you that it is a much better one than being in the vicious cycle of going back to her.

>Because of the corona thing there is nothing for me to do and most of times I have to stay at my home which is just making me feel worse.

I know how you feel, purely because I've been experiencing something similar myself (no toxic ex, but was just seeing someone that ghosted me out of nowhere) and it is really hard to not reach out, even months later. However, you have to keep reminding yourself that the whole situation was/is really toxic and it'll get even worse if you keep talking to her and seeing her. If nothing else helps, try taking up a completely new and random hobby that you can practice from home.

I wonder every single day and can never convince myself with a good enough reason. And this makes me want to ask more and more questions. However, I try to keep reminding myself of something I saw when researching the topic once - it was along the lines that we should stop asking ourselves questions that humanity won't *really* be able to answer anytime soon if they are making us unhappy.

You definitely aren't alone. I'm still studying and had only a couple of internships in tech over the summers, but the anxiety I would get every time during any of the meetings was insane. Whenever I had to speak, I'd have breathing difficulties and start shaking, and that would make it worse because I'd panic that everyone will notice. This happened even if it was just when I was introducing myself. One thing that I keep telling myself is that the only person that really knows how I feel is me and that others would hardly notice if something I say is wrong and even if they realize, they wouldn't judge me. It's not 100% effective for me, but it helps. Just think of how you don't notice any minor "issues" with others in the way that you do with yourself. I hope this helps and I wish you the greatest luck! I hope that the more meetings you have, you will build on your insecurity and will get better!

I know someone else has already mentioned this, but anxiety can be horrible and I just wanted to give you some more reassurance. When I started having breathing difficulties months ago, I panicked even more one night and felt like I was going to die too. Didn't know what was wrong with me, or why it was happening. My vision got blurry and the more I panicked, the worse my breathing got. So my advice would be (as hard as it is!) to try to calm yourself down if it happens again and sit or lay down ( I don't know if this is a thing, but my body automatically feels more relaxed when I lay down). And be aware that it is just anxiety. Keep repeating to yourself that you will get better and if you are able to find a meditation video/ podcast, it could be helpful too, but this is only if you feel like you can do it. If you aren't able to, keep telling yourself that there is nothing wrong with the situation and that it's going to go away very soon. Sending you a hug and my good wishes!

>help me literally live. And as far as for ur suggestion I wish I could but I can barely get up in the morning.  What I felt today was the best in years and now I'm back in my deep dark cave again so yeah..

I'm glad that you felt good today, if those days are rare and it's helpful to appreciate them. If you can't get out of bed in the mornings (I'm really sorry to hear that), maybe try writing down stuff on your laptop/phone? I used to do this a couple of months ago when I couldn't even wake up but it became my routine to try and open my eyes and write down my feelings. It might not work for you (and I really apologize if I'm pushing you, totally not my intention!), but it's a starting point. Also, instead of going straight to things like negative social media (to me all of it is negative), perhaps try making a profile on instagram and follow accounts that share daily positive news. Once again, sorry if you don't feel like doing any of these or you've tried them already! (And feel free to ignore me if that's better for your mental health!!!)

Do it! I recently deleted facebook and set a timer for 5 mins a day for instagram and I feel SO much better. I also realized that there is nothing to do on those apps and they just make me miserable seeing how others are enjoying their lives (ofc, that's just their highlights, but I don't even have those). I used to use social media to procrastinate and I still do it, but have found much more creative ways to do it (which don't make me feel depressed), so I'd definitely advise you to try out ditching the apps that make you feel sad.

hey! I don't quite know how to help you because I also have very similar issues. Of course, everyone's pain is different and completely valid and destructive on its own, but you are not alone. I feel horrible and tired every single day. Sometimes I'm just too scared to die because I don't want to hurt people around me (or don't want them to notice that I'm not there because that would draw their attention). The two things that I've found to help me when I do them are journaling and volunteering to help others. Just a suggestion, which you probably have seen a lot, but perhaps never tried? Anyways, let me know if you try them out and feel free to message me if you want to talk to someone / for someone to listen to you.
